t: This is Gayfere Lodge, a terrace house in Westminster. It was designed by Oliver Hill, an architect, landscape architect and garden designer. Hill began as a follower of Edwin Lutyens, and in the 1920s became known for country houses. In the 1930s he turned towards modernism, while still valuing natural materials, and he liked curving lines. He also designed the Midland Hotel in Morecambe and the British pavilion at the Paris Exposition of 1937.
